title: Anger and Fear
human_question: What happens in us when life refuses what we want?
journey: Chathura meets conflict, loss, rivalry, envy and fear: places marked by disputes, disasters, and people living with regret.
surface: Frustration, envy, fear and remorse, seen through real consequences in real lives, never staged.
depth: The two hate-rooted minds always arise with displeasure, so anger is its own suffering, felt first by the one who is angry. The fourteen unwholesome factors (envy, stinginess, remorse, conceit, wrong view and others) and how they combine in each unwholesome mind.

arc.opening: Something pushes back. Object 3 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Anger, envy, stinginess, worry: each seen as a cost carried by the person who holds it.
arc.closing: After the heat, a fog: not knowing which way to go.

hands_off: When the heat fades, what remains is confusion.

lesson.in_simple_terms: When life refuses what we want, the mind pushes back: as anger, fear, possessiveness, or a heaviness that will not move. The texts describe every form of this pushing-away as painful to the one who feels it first, and never joyful, even when it feels justified. When the heat fades, what is left is often not calm but a fog of not knowing which way to go.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ජීවිතය අප කැමති දේ නොදුන් විට සිත තරහ, බිය, මසුරුකම හෝ බර ගතියක් ලෙස ඊට එරෙහිව නැගී සිටින බවත්, ඒ සෑම එකක්ම මුලින්ම දුකක් වන්නේ එය දැනෙන කෙනාටම බවත් ධර්මය කියයි. ඒ උණුසුම නිවී ගිය පසු බොහෝ විට ඉතිරි වන්නේ සන්සුන් බවක් නොව, යා යුතු මඟ නොදන්නා මීදුමකි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma counts two hate-rooted states of mind; both always come with a painful mental feeling and never with joy, and they differ only in whether they arise on their own or are urged along. Under the one word 'hate' the texts gather anger, fear, dislike and discontent, and they name not getting what one wants among its most common occasions. Envy, stinginess and remorse arise only with this aversion, one at a time, and stinginess, though born of attachment, shows itself as displeasure at sharing. Around them the fourteen unwholesome factors fill in the picture: delusion and restlessness are present in every harmful moment, wrong view and conceit are two grips that never share a moment, and dullness appears only in a mind that had to be pushed.
progression: EPD-0019 The Mended Net: blocked wanting turns against whatever stands in its way, and the pain of it is felt first by the one who is angry.
EPD-0020 The Watch Hut: fear belongs to the same family as anger, the same pushing-away once a threat seems too strong.
EPD-0021 The Even Share: holding on to what is ours shows itself as displeasure at sharing, which is why the texts group it with aversion.
EPD-0022 The Closed Hand: that holding back can cling to knowledge and skill, not only to things.
EPD-0023 Held Up: even a small, ordinary refusal sets off displeasure, and a restless mind that will not settle.
EPD-0024 Which Word Carries the Water: clinging to a view and clinging to one's standing are two different grips that never share a moment.
EPD-0025 Willing Hands: heaviness and dullness belong to a mind that had to be pushed, not to one that moved on its own.
EPD-0026 What the Body Remembers: anger never carries joy and burns its holder first, which is why the texts advise living watchfully.
EPD-0027 Not Yet Decided: when the heat fades, a mind that cannot settle is left, and ordinary uncertainty is not a fault.
lesson.builds_on: The previous stage followed wanting from the pleasant feeling where it begins, and showed that it can come with joy; this stage picks up where wanting is blocked and turns into aversion, which the texts say never comes with joy.
lesson.hands_to_next: Having found delusion and restlessness underneath every flare of heat, and ending in a household that cannot settle, the group hands on the question of what it is that stops us seeing clearly once the heat has gone and only confusion remains.
